92	def plot_reliability_diagram(confidences, accuracies, n_bins=10,
93	                              label='', color='#0072B2',
94	                              title='Reliability Diagram',
95	                              outpath='reliability.pdf'):
96	    """
97	    confidences, accuracies: 各样本的 confidence 和 binary correct (0/1)
98	    """
99	    bin_edges = np.linspace(0, 1, n_bins + 1)
100	    bin_accs, bin_confs, bin_counts = [], [], []
101	
102	    for i in range(n_bins):
103	        lo, hi = bin_edges[i], bin_edges[i+1]
104	        mask = (confidences >= lo) & (confidences < hi)
105	        if mask.sum() > 0:
106	            bin_accs.append(accuracies[mask].mean())
107	            bin_confs.append(confidences[mask].mean())
108	            bin_counts.append(mask.sum())
109	        else:
110	            bin_accs.append(float('nan'))
111	            bin_confs.append((lo + hi) / 2)
112	            bin_counts.append(0)
113	
114	    bin_accs = np.array(bin_accs)
115	    bin_confs = np.array(bin_confs)
116	
117	    fig, (ax_main, ax_hist) = plt.subplots(
118	        2, 1, figsize=(4, 4.5), gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [3, 1]},
119	        sharex=True
120	    )
121	
122	    # 主图：gaps
123	    ax_main.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_accs, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
124	                color=color, alpha=0.7, label='Accuracy', zorder=2)
125	    ax_main.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_confs - bin_accs, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
126	                bottom=bin_accs, color='red', alpha=0.3, label='Gap', zorder=2)
127	    ax_main.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], 'k--', linewidth=1, zorder=3, label='Perfect')
128	    ax_main.set_xlim(0, 1); ax_main.set_ylim(0, 1)
129	    ax_main.set_ylabel('Accuracy')
130	    ax_main.set_title(title)
131	    ax_main.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=9)
132	    ax_main.grid(True, alpha=0.3, zorder=1)
133	
134	    # ECE annotation
135	    ece = np.nansum(np.array(bin_counts) / sum(bin_counts) *
136	                    np.abs(bin_accs - bin_confs))
137	    ax_main.text(0.98, 0.02, f'ECE={ece:.3f}', transform=ax_main.transAxes,
138	                 ha='right', va='bottom', fontsize=9,
139	                 bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='white', alpha=0.8))
140

143	                color=color, alpha=0.5)

```python
def plot_reliability_diagram(confidences, accuracies, n_bins=10,
                              label='', color='#0072B2',
                              title='Reliability Diagram',
                              outpath='reliability.pdf'):
    """
    confidences, accuracies: 各样本的 confidence 和 binary correct (0/1)
    """
    bin_edges = np.linspace(0, 1, n_bins + 1)
    bin_accs, bin_confs, bin_counts = [], [], []

    for i in range(n_bins):
        lo, hi = bin_edges[i], bin_edges[i+1]
        mask = (confidences >= lo) & (confidences < hi)
        if mask.sum() > 0:
            bin_accs.append(accuracies[mask].mean())
            bin_confs.append(confidences[mask].mean())
            bin_counts.append(mask.sum())
        else:
            bin_accs.append(float('nan'))
            bin_confs.append((lo + hi) / 2)
            bin_counts.append(0)

    bin_accs = np.array(bin_accs)
    bin_confs = np.array(bin_confs)

    fig, (ax_main, ax_hist) = plt.subplots(
        2, 1, figsize=(4, 4.5), gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [3, 1]},
        sharex=True
    )

    # 主图：gaps
    ax_main.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_accs, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
                color=color, alpha=0.7, label='Accuracy', zorder=2)
    ax_main.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_confs - bin_accs, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
                bottom=bin_accs, color='red', alpha=0.3, label='Gap', zorder=2)
    ax_main.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], 'k--', linewidth=1, zorder=3, label='Perfect')
    ax_main.set_xlim(0, 1); ax_main.set_ylim(0, 1)
    ax_main.set_ylabel('Accuracy')
    ax_main.set_title(title)
    ax_main.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=9)
    ax_main.grid(True, alpha=0.3, zorder=1)

    # ECE annotation
    ece = np.nansum(np.array(bin_counts) / sum(bin_counts) *
                    np.abs(bin_accs - bin_confs))
    ax_main.text(0.98, 0.02, f'ECE={ece:.3f}', transform=ax_main.transAxes,
                 ha='right', va='bottom', fontsize=9,
                 bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='white', alpha=0.8))

    # 直方图（样本密度）
    ax_hist.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_counts, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
                color=color, alpha=0.5)
    ax_hist.set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=9)
    ax_hist.set_xlabel('Confidence')

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(outpath)
    plt.close()
    print(f'Saved: {outpath}')
```

```python
def plot_ece_heatmap(delta_ece_matrix, methods, datasets,
                     title='ΔECE Heatmap (vs FP16)',
                     outpath='ece_heatmap.pdf'):
    """
    delta_ece_matrix: shape (n_methods, n_datasets), 正=ECE 恶化, 负=改善
    """
    import matplotlib.colors as mcolors

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(len(datasets) * 1.2, len(methods) * 0.8 + 1))

    # 发散色图（中心=0, 红=恶化, 蓝=改善）
    vmax = np.nanmax(np.abs(delta_ece_matrix))
    norm = mcolors.TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-vmax, vcenter=0, vmax=vmax)
    cmap = plt.cm.RdBu_r

    im = ax.imshow(delta_ece_matrix, cmap=cmap, norm=norm, aspect='auto')

    # 数值标注
    for i in range(len(methods)):
        for j in range(len(datasets)):
            val = delta_ece_matrix[i, j]
            if not np.isnan(val):
                color = 'white' if abs(val) > vmax * 0.6 else 'black'
                sign = '+' if val > 0 else ''
                ax.text(j, i, f'{sign}{val:.1%}', ha='center', va='center',
                        fontsize=9, color=color, fontweight='bold')

    ax.set_xticks(range(len(datasets)))
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(methods)))
    ax.set_xticklabels(datasets, rotation=30, ha='right')
    ax.set_yticklabels(methods)
    ax.set_title(title)

    cbar = plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.046, pad=0.04)
    cbar.set_label('ΔECE (quantized − FP16)')
    cbar.ax.axhline(0, color='k', linewidth=0.8)

    print(f'Saved: {outpath}')
```

**SDF regression loss.** The first auxiliary loss encourages the SDF head to accurately predict signed distances from the model's internal features:

$$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SDF}} = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{V}|} \sum_{(i,j) \in \mathcal{V}} \left(\hat{s}_{i,j} - s_{i,j}\right)^2,$$

where $\mathcal{V}$ is the set of valid sample-timestep pairs with available ground-truth labels, $\hat{s}_{i,j}$ is the predicted signed distance, and $s_{i,j}$ is the ground truth. This loss ensures the auxiliary head provides a faithful geometric probe of the model's representations, which in turn supplies meaningful gradients for the collision penalty.

**Collision penalty loss.** The second auxiliary loss penalizes predictions that fall below the safety margin $\delta$:

$$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{col}} = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{V}|} \sum_{(i,j) \in \mathcal{V}} w(t_i) \cdot \mathrm{ReLU}\!\left(\delta - \hat{s}_{i,j}\right),$$

where $\delta = 0.02\,\mathrm{m}$ (2cm safety margin) and $t_i$ is the flow-matching timestep for sample $i$. The ReLU activation ensures that only near-collision and penetrating states are penalized: when $\hat{s}_{i,j} > \delta$, the contribution is zero; when $\hat{s}_{i,j} < \delta$, the penalty grows linearly with the depth of violation. Combined with the noise-aware weight $w(t_i)$, this loss selectively shapes the velocity field in the low-noise regime where the model's action predictions are geometrically meaningful.

**Total training objective.** The complete loss combines the flow-matching objective with both auxiliary terms:

$$\mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{FM}} + \lambda_{\mathrm{SDF}} \cdot \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SDF}} + \lambda_{\mathrm{col}} \cdot \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{col}},$$

where $\lambda_{\mathrm{SDF}} = 0.1$ and $\lambda_{\mathrm{col}} = 0.01$. The relatively small weight on the collision term reflects its role as a shaping signal rather than a hard constraint: the primary training signal remains the flow-matching loss, and the collision penalty gently steers the learned velocity field toward safer regions without dominating the optimization.


### 3.4 Training Pipeline

GeoSafe training follows the standard $\pi_{0.5}$ fine-tuning pipeline with minimal modifications. The base model is initialized from pretrained $\pi_{0.5}$ weights. We perform full fine-tuning of all parameters (not LoRA), as the 96GB VRAM per GPU provides sufficient capacity and full fine-tuning yields a stronger baseline for evaluating the incremental effect of collision shaping.

**Gradient flow through the backbone.** A critical design choice is whether to allow gradients from the SDF losses to propagate back through the action expert. When $\hat{s} = \mathrm{SDFHead}(f_t)$ with $f_t$ treated as a leaf tensor (detached from the computation graph), the SDF losses train only the auxiliary head to predict distances accurately but do not influence action generation. To test our core hypothesis that collision-shaping can modify the velocity field itself, we enable gradient flow from the SDF head through the shared features $f_t$ into the action expert weights. Concretely, the feature tensor $f_t$ captured by the forward hook is used without detachment, so that $\nabla_{f_t} \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SDF}}$ and $\nabla_{f_t} \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{col}}$ both contribute to the backbone parameter update. This is the mechanism by which safety awareness becomes embedded in the model's action generation process.

**Optimization.** We use the AdamW optimizer with the same hyperparameters as the base $\pi_{0.5}$ configuration. The SDF head parameters are added to the same optimizer with shared learning rate and weight decay. Gradients from all parameters (base model and SDF head jointly) are clipped by global norm with $\mathrm{max\_norm} = 1.0$. For the [PLACEHOLDER]-step training runs, we use a linear warmup of [PLACEHOLDER] steps. Training uses PyTorch Distributed Data Parallel (DDP) across multiple GPUs, with gradient averaging for both the base model and SDF head parameters. The per-GPU batch size is 64, yielding an effective batch size of 128 on 2 GPUs.

**Data augmentation with SDF labels.** The training data pipeline wraps the standard $\pi_{0.5}$ data loader. The `SDFAugmentedDataset` class intercepts each training sample after all standard transforms (image preprocessing, action normalization, prompt construction) and appends the corresponding SDF labels by looking up the precomputed `SDFLabelStore` using the sample's task index, episode index, and frame index. Samples without matching SDF labels are marked as invalid and excluded from the SDF loss computation, ensuring that the flow-matching loss is unaffected by label coverage gaps. In total, SDF labels cover 57 tasks across 8 task suites: the four standard LIBERO suites (LIBERO-Spatial, LIBERO-Object, LIBERO-Goal, LIBERO-10) have full coverage (10/10 tasks each), while the four SafeLIBERO suites have partial coverage (4 to 5 tasks each). Each task provides 50 demonstrations with per-timestep signed distance annotations, yielding labels for approximately 75\% of all training tasks.


### 3.5 Inference

At inference time, the SDF auxiliary head is discarded entirely. The trained model is served using the standard $\pi_{0.5}$ inference pipeline, with the same checkpoint format and serving infrastructure. No SDF computation, distance queries, or collision checking is performed during deployment. The model generates actions by integrating its learned velocity field through the standard ODE solver, exactly as the unmodified $\pi_{0.5}$ would. The safety behavior manifests through the modified model weights: the collision-shaping training signal has adjusted the velocity field to naturally produce trajectories that maintain clearance from obstacles.

This property distinguishes GeoSafe from inference-time safety methods such as runtime trajectory filtering, control barrier functions, or guided sampling. These approaches add computational overhead proportional to the number of denoising steps or constraint evaluations, and may require access to the scene geometry at deployment. GeoSafe incurs zero additional latency, zero additional memory, and requires no geometric information at test time.

**Connection to guidance distillation.** Our approach bears a structural analogy to guidance distillation in diffusion models. In classifier-guided diffusion, an external classifier provides a gradient signal $\nabla_{x_t} \log p(y | x_t)$ that steers the sampling process toward a desired class $y$. Guidance distillation trains a single model to reproduce the effect of this guidance without requiring the classifier at inference. Similarly, GeoSafe uses the SDF auxiliary head as a "geometric safety classifier" that provides a training-time gradient signal directing the velocity field away from collision regions. After training, the model has internalized this signal, and the auxiliary head (analogous to the classifier) is no longer needed. Unlike classical guidance distillation, which replicates a guided sampling trajectory during training, our method shapes the velocity field directly through auxiliary gradients. The SDF head provides a training-time geometric signal that modifies the learned flow rather than distilling a pre-computed guided process. A further difference is that our method operates in the flow-matching framework rather than score-based diffusion, and the guidance signal comes from geometric structure (signed distances) rather than semantic class labels.

                linestyle='-', linewidth=1.0, zorder=2, text=None,
                fontsize=7.5, fontcolor='black', fontweight='normal', text_y_offset=0):
    if edgecolor is None:
        edgecolor = color
    box = FancyBboxPatch((x, y), w, h,
                         boxstyle="round,pad=0.08",
                         facecolor=color, edgecolor=edgecolor,
                         linewidth=linewidth, linestyle=linestyle,
                         alpha=alpha, zorder=zorder,
                         mutation_scale=0.3)
    ax.add_patch(box)
    if text:
        ax.text(x + w/2, y + h/2 + text_y_offset, text,
                ha='center', va='center', fontsize=fontsize,
                color=fontcolor, fontweight=fontweight, zorder=zorder+1)
    return box

def arrow(ax, x1, y1, x2, y2, color='#333333', linewidth=1.0,
          linestyle='-', zorder=3, arrowstyle='->', mutation_scale=10):

                         arrowstyle=arrowstyle,
                         color=color, linewidth=linewidth,
                         linestyle=linestyle, zorder=zorder,
                         mutation_scale=mutation_scale,

    ax.add_patch(ar)
    return ar
